title: Lua Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: print shows a value and moves to a new line.

examples.title: Keep a local value
examples.description: local limits a name to its part of the program. This helps avoid accidental global names.

examples.title: Join text
examples.description: Two dots join text in Lua. Joining text is called concatenation.

examples.title: Choose a message
examples.description: if checks a condition. then starts its steps and end closes them.
examples.code:
local score = 8
if score >= 5 then
 print("Pass")
else
 print("Try again")
end

examples.title: Use a table as a list
examples.description: A table can act as an ordered list. The usual first position is 1.

examples.title: Use named table fields
examples.description: A table can also pair names with values. A dot reads a named field.
examples.code:
local book = { title = "Moon Trip", pages = 24 }
print(book.title)

examples.title: Count with a for loop
examples.description: A numeric for loop includes both its start and end values.

examples.title: Visit list items
examples.description: ipairs gives a position and value for list-style entries starting at 1.
examples.code:
for _, pet in ipairs({"cat", "dog"}) do
 print(pet)
end

examples.title: Return a result
examples.description: A function is a named group of steps. return sends a value back.
examples.code:
local function twice(n)
 return n * 2
end
print(twice(4))

examples.title: Use a fallback
examples.description: nil means no value. or chooses the second value when the first is nil or false.

examples.title: Return two values
examples.description: Lua functions can return several values. A matching assignment reads them.
examples.code:
local function pair()
 return 3, 5
end
local a, b = pair()
print(a + b)

examples.title: Catch a failed call
examples.description: pcall runs a function and reports whether it succeeded. The first result is true or false.
examples.code:
local ok = pcall(function() error("Try again") end)
print(ok)
